exposure: Maternal time of rupture of membrane > 12 hours before delivery
cohort: 380 neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Bombe Primary Hospital from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019
finding: The study found a high neonatal mortality rate (20.8 per 1000 neonatal days) and identified late initiation of early breastfeeding, low APGAR score, low birth weight, hypothermia, and prolonged rupture of membranes as risk factors for neonatal death.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with a decreased risk of neonatal mortality.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was a significant predictor of neonatal mortality.
